To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dyad G box in the Adh gene is a target of a trans-acting protein in vivo and in Arabidopsis cell culture and leaves, but the G-box protein is present in both cell culture and leaf extracts, and in leaves the G-box protein does not bind to the Adh gene in vivo.
the G-box element in the Arabidopsis thalina Adh gene is bound by a protein in vitro and in vivo, and this binding is not directly correlated with the tissue in which this gene is expressed.

the G-box is associated with Adh gene expression in Arabidopsis, that the G-box factor can be detected in crude whole cell extract of both leaves and cell culture, and that the Adh G- box factor does not bind to its target site in vivo in leaves, but does bind in cell culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of protein factors that are associated with the Adh G box.
the characterization of a G-box protein that binds to the Adh gene and the identification of the G-box protein in vivo.
the in vivo and in vitr characterization of protein binding to a G-box in the promoter of the Adh gene of A. thaliana.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Adh G box binds a trans-acting protein factor(s) in vivo and in vivo.
the Adh G-Box factor is not a transcription factor, but is an important component of a complex of proteins involved with Adh expression.
the in vitro Adh binding activity is a true in vivo factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Adh G box is bound by a trans-acting complex that is present in both cell culture and leaf extracts, but that the G-box binding complex may be different in the two tissue extracts.
the Adh G box is a binding site for a protein(s) in vitro and that this binding activity is associated with a protein factor in vivo.
the Adh G-Box is associated with an inducible trans-acting protein factor in vivo and in extracts of both cell cultures and leaves of Arabdopsis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a protein in both cell culture and leaf extracts that binds to a sequence that is similar to the light-inducible G-box of RbcS.
the Adh G-Box factor is not tissue-specific, and that the Adh and RbcS G-box factors may be different.
the Adh G box is a binding site for the same factor that binds the RbcS G-box, which is a light-inducible factor.
